purpose: Iterate a diverse game-theoretic sparring ladder aimed at improving transfer to strong unseen sumo humans. Nomophobia is one developing player's style, always development only. Draw practical hypotheses from first-person recordings of winning and losing exchanges, then test them with matched actions and full round ring-outs.
families: Maintain plain W-tap and continuous-W controls, explicit sprint/contact rules, distance and injury-window spacing, hit selection, edge recovery, local lookahead over input words, nearest-prototype tactical tables, and affine/MLP/recurrent learned fighters. Each contender sees only its own client. The lookahead estimates a small local game under multiple plausible opponent actions; it cannot read actual future timing or server poses. Explicit policies expose their rule names, input words and parameters.
iteration: Twelve alternating seasons. Within EACH season search both an explicit tactical response and a neural response against the previous pool. Keep diverse opponent families and sample weaknesses exposed in the preceding cross-play. Re-evaluate new representatives in a tournament with old champions, update the opponent pool and log which opponents and match situations drive the next round. Save results even if an iteration regresses. Include human-timing sparring as one small family, alongside independently trained adversaries and programmed strategies. Keep older representatives to test forgetting. Champion snapshots at seasons 1, 4, 8, 12 go to main-lab transfer. A separate native selection and frozen confirmation decide the playable entry.
examples: Use only original 16 simulator training calendars and already exposed development material to fit. Prototype centers may come from the locked human fit rounds and actual simulator states from training clocks. Repeated development tournaments use original eight selection donors. All native future donors for an individual stage are frozen in advance, and the final confirmation uses eight newly recorded mirror donor calendars and independent, seat- and RTT-balanced Minecraft bouts. Show W-tap and Hold-W alongside every contender.
objectives: Rank regulation matches by actual ring-out, double falls or timeout give half a point. Equal-weight opponent families and worst-family score. Score boxing separately, including on complete common-state maintenance forks. Diagnose any weak explicit or learned approach versus W-tap before making it more complex. Hindsight continuations and native debug traces can supply offline labels only.
